thread:
nina: Heads-up: our onboarding sample app (Go + node combo) started failing CI on rerank assertions after we updated to the new client. Getting `expected_dim=1536 got=1535` on some runs but only for a tiny fraction of inputs. Any ideas?

nina: repro steps (summary):
- run `make ci-sampleapp` on branch `feature/sdk-parity`
- send batch of 12 documents through embed helper -> embeddings.create -> rerank
- rerank fails for 1 item with dim mismatch

nina: logged the embeddings array length right after the SDK returns: `len=1535`. Model is `embed-3b` (1536 dims).

omar: can you paste the raw payload you POSTed to rerank (trimmed)? Need to check whether the SDK is serializing `embedding` vs `embedding_bytes` and whether it's nested correctly.

nina: trimmed body: `{"queries":[[0.001, -0.002, ..., 0.09]], "candidates":[[[...]]]}`. It looks like arrays, not bytes.

felix: couple of things we've seen recently: 1) JS helper had a bug where last-chunk padding used `buffer.length` instead of `buffer.byteLength` when converting Float32->Uint8, dropping final 4 bytes for some alignments; 2) Go SDK introduced an alias renaming `embedding` -> `vec` in the v0.10 experimental build which confused some downstream code that still expects `embedding`. Which SDKs are in play?

nina: test matrix: go-sdk v0.10 (sampleapp), node-sdk v1.3 (backend), model serve is hosted. The failing item originated in Go path.

omar: okay. Two quick checks: a) is the Go SDK emitting `embedding` (array) or `embedding_bytes`? b) if bytes, what's its length % 4? If arrays, is the last element missing or NaN?

nina: i added debug prints. output: `field=vec_bytes len=6143 bytes %4 = 3`. That looks wrong.

felix: that explains it. 6143 bytes -> 1535 floats after unpack. Bug is in the Go base64 encoder path: it was using `buf := buffer[:n-1]` in a streaming chunk close routine on Windows builds to "strip null frame" which accidentally strips a byte when chunk size is exact multiple minus one due to an off-by-one in the chunker.

nina: yikes. So the server accepts `embedding_bytes` but when clients unpack they get 1535 floats and rerank rejects. Workaround on our side: detect `vec_bytes` len %4 != 0 and pad with zeros before unpack. Quick patch we used: `if len(b)%4 != 0 { b = append(b, bytes.Repeat([]byte{0}, 4-(len(b)%4))...) }`

omar: action items suggested:
- devex: revert `vec` alias in Go SDK to `embedding` to avoid field-name churn until parity is fully coordinated. Add warning in changelog.
- devex: patch Go SDK chunker to not drop the trailing byte and add unit test for odd-size streaming output.
- eng-runtime: when validating rerank payloads, return structured diagnostics: {"expected_dim":1536, "got":1535, "field":"queries[4]","bytes_mod_4":3} so clients can map easily.
- devex: add a quick check helper `ensureEmbeddingDims(embedding, model)` in SDKs that throws early with guidance instead of letting rerank fail obscurely.

felix: i'll open INF-6220 with the Go fix and INF-6221 for the SDK field parity revert. I'll also add a tiny CLI check in the sampleapp that asserts dims before sending.

sdk-bot: Created INF-6220: "go sdk chunker strips trailing byte on windows stream close" assigned to @felix. Created INF-6221: "sdk parity: revert vec->embedding alias until coordinated" assigned to @omar.

nina: i validated local patch (pad bytes before unpack) and CI passed for the previously failing run. Will watch for nightly flakiness.

omar: one more note for everyone: sometimes the embedding is returned as `embedding` array (floats) and sometimes as `embedding_bytes` (base64). If you rely on one form, make sure the SDK normalizes both to a canonical `embedding` array before you call rerank. We'll add that to the sampleapp README and the onboarding checklist.

felix: agreed. Also adding a tiny snippet for folks:
```js
// defensive check before rerank
function normalizeEmbedding(item, dim) {
  if (item.embedding) return item.embedding;
  if (item.embedding_bytes) {
    let b = base64ToUint8(item.embedding_bytes);
    if (b.length % 4 !== 0) b = padZero(b, 4 - (b.length % 4));
    return float32ArrayFromBytes(b);
  }
  throw new Error('missing embedding');
}
```

nina: thanks all. Leaving this thread for anyone who hits onboarding flakiness. Will reopen if we see more failures. :thumbsup:
